title: If I were you
goal: Talk about imaginary situations with if + past, would
intro: To talk about something unreal or unlikely now, use if + past, then would: “If I had more time, I would learn the piano.” The past form here doesn’t mean the past; it means “not real”. With be, careful English uses “were” for everyone: “If I were you…”.

rules.rule: Unreal now: if + past, would + verb.
examples: If I won the lottery, I would travel.
If he lived closer, we’d meet more.

rules.rule: If I were you, I’d… is the classic way to give advice.
examples: If I were you, I’d take the job.
If she were here, she’d know.
If I knew, I’d tell you.
If we had a car, we’d drive.

mistakes.wrong: If I would have money, I would buy it.
mistakes.right: If I had money, I would buy it.

mistakes.wrong: If I am you, I will go.
mistakes.right: If I were you, I would go.
mistakes.why: Advice: If I were you, I’d…

mistakes.wrong: If I knew, I will tell you.
mistakes.right: If I knew, I would tell you.

mistakes.wrong: If she was here, she would helped.
mistakes.right: If she were here, she would help.

ex.q: If I ___ rich, I’d buy a big house.
If I were you, I ___ call her.
If she ___ how to drive, she’d go alone.
What would you do if you ___ a million dollars?
If I would know his number, I would call him.
ex.fixed: If I knew his number, I would call him.

ex.q: If I am you, I would apologize.
ex.fixed: If I were you, I would apologize.

ex.q: If we had a garden, we will grow vegetables.
ex.fixed: If we had a garden, we would grow vegetables.

ex.q: If I ___ (be) taller, I would play basketball.

ex.a: If I were you, I would talk to him.
ex.y: If I were you, I would…

ex.q: Give advice starting with “If I were you”: your friend is always tired.
a: If I were you I would*
ex.y: If I were you, I’d sleep earlier.

talk: Answer these imaginary questions: If you could live anywhere, where would you live? If you had a free year, what would you do? If you were the prime minister, what would you change?
